web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Machine — Upstream, Midstream & Global LNG
question: How do EQT's three reportable segments—Upstream, Gathering, and Transmission—combine with its emerging LNG marketing book to convert Appalachian shale molecules into cash flow?

epigraph.quote: When you own both the rock and the pipe beneath it, every dollar of gathering inefficiency you eliminate drops straight to consolidated free cash flow.
epigraph.author: Integrated Energy Operating Principle

web_blocks.html: After buying Equitrans Midstream in July 2024, EQT reorganized its reporting into three segments in its FY2025 Form 10-K: Upstream (formerly Production), Gathering, and Transmission [1]. Together, these three units generated $8,644.2 million in operating revenue in FY2025 [1, 2]. They also delivered $3,249.6 million in operating income on 2,382 Bcfe of total sales volume [1, 2].

web_blocks.takeaway: While Upstream remains the primary earnings engine ($2,318.1M operating income in FY2025), Gathering and Transmission contributed $1,211.9M in combined segment operating income, buffering cash flows during soft gas-price quarters [1].

web_blocks.html: 1. Upstream Segment (2,382 Bcfe in FY2025): EQT's Upstream unit explores for and produces natural gas, NGLs, and oil in the Marcellus and Utica shales [1]. Its wells span Pennsylvania, West Virginia, and Ohio [1]. At December 31, 2025, EQT held 28,046 Bcfe (~28.0 Tcfe) of proved reserves [1]. Roughly 93% sits in the Marcellus Shale [1]. By state, reserves break down into Pennsylvania (17,253 Bcfe), West Virginia (9,927 Bcfe), and Ohio (866 Bcfe) [1]. About 73% (20,581 Bcfe) are proved developed, and 27% (7,465 Bcfe) are proved undeveloped [1]. Sales of gas, NGLs, and oil reached $7,726.7 million in FY2025 [1]. The average realized price was $3.19/Mcfe including settled hedges [1, 2].

Concrete End-to-End Upstream Example: Picture a multi-well combo pad in Greene County, Pennsylvania. EQT's team drills 15,000-foot horizontal wells into the Marcellus Shale ~7,000 feet underground [1]. Crews fracture the rock using recycled water and regional sand [1]. Raw wet gas flows to a central pad separator where water and condensate drop out. Dry gas and NGLs are metered and sold at local hubs like Eastern Gas South, or shipped via firm pipe to Gulf Coast and Mid-Atlantic utilities. Utilities such as Duke Energy or Dominion Energy buy firm winter baseload gas tied to Henry Hub or Transco Zone 5. That locks in multi-year supply while EQT pockets the spread above its ~$2.00/MMBtu unlevered breakeven [3, 8].

2. Gathering Segment ($836.7M Operating Income in FY2025): Through XcL Midstream (2023) and Equitrans (2024), EQT owns thousands of miles of low- and high-pressure gathering lines [1, 7, 14]. It also runs dehydration units and compressor stations across southwestern Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia [1, 7, 14]. About 76% of Gathering revenue comes from moving EQT's own Upstream gas [1]. The other ~24% comes from third-party drillers paying fixed per-Mcf gathering and compression fees [1].

Concrete End-to-End Gathering Example: Suppose a third-party driller in Wetzel County, West Virginia brings a new pad online without local pipe. Raw wellhead gas at 300–500 psi cannot enter a 1,200-psi interstate line. EQT's Gathering unit ties the wellhead into its header network. Electric-drive stations compress the gas, strip out water, and deliver it to interstate interconnects. EQT collects a fixed, inflation-linked fee per Mcf, turning its existing pipe grid into a steady tollbooth [1, 7].

3. Transmission Segment & Emerging LNG Marketing ($375.2M Operating Income in FY2025; $286.8M in 9M 2026): EQT's Transmission unit runs FERC-regulated interstate pipes, underground storage, and the Hammerhead Pipeline [1, 10, 18]. It also operates its stake in the 303-mile, 2.0 Bcf/d Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP) [1, 10, 18]. About 61% of Transmission revenue serves EQT Upstream, while ~39% serves outside utilities under firm contracts [1]. Beyond the 2.5 MTPA NextDecade (1.5 MTPA) and Commonwealth LNG (1.0 MTPA) deals, the FY2025 Form 10-K discloses up to 6.5 MTPA of 20-year LNG commitments [1, 11, 12]. That totals 4.5 MTPA of offtake plus up to 2.0 MTPA of tolling starting 2030–2031, though 3.0 MTPA awaits project FID [1]. In Q3 2026, EQT also signed a 10-year LNG sales contract with Lithuania's Ignitis Group, leased 7 Bcf of Leaf River Gulf Coast salt-dome storage (reaching 11 Bcf total), and launched an open season for the 42-inch POWER Pipeline to Clarington, Ohio.

Concrete End-to-End Transmission & LNG Example: A power utility in North Carolina or a European LNG buyer faces winter supply risk because Appalachian gas is often trapped behind local bottlenecks. EQT routes gas from northern West Virginia onto MVP (2.0 Bcf/d capacity) down to Station 165 in Pittsylvania County, Virginia [8, 18]. From there, it feeds Transco Zone 5 markets [8, 18]. Under its 2025 LNG SPAs, EQT holds Gulf Coast liquefaction slots. It delivers Henry Hub-priced feedgas and sells cargoes to European or Asian buyers tied to TTF or JKM, keeping the global spread without middleman fees [11, 12].

web_blocks.title: Why Intersegment Eliminations Matter for Analytical Clarity
paragraphs: Because Upstream pays Gathering and Transmission internal fees, summing segment operating incomes ($2,318.1M + $836.7M + $375.2M = $3,530.0M) exceeds consolidated operating income ($3,249.6M) after corporate overhead and intersegment eliminations [1]. On a consolidated basis, however, EQT retains the third-party midstream profit while reducing its effective per-unit Upstream gathering cost.

web_blocks.html: Segment data in the FY2025 Form 10-K show how vertical integration dampens earnings swings [1]. Upstream operating income jumped from $403.6 million in FY2024 to $2,318.1 million in FY2025 [1]. Realized prices recovered to $3.19/Mcfe on 2,382 Bcfe of sales volume, up from 2,228 Bcfe in FY2024 after the July 2025 Olympus Energy close [1, 2, 13]. Gathering earned $836.7 million in FY2025 operating income, up from $531.5 million in FY2024 and $128.6 million in FY2023 [1]. Transmission added $375.2 million in FY2025, up from $140.8 million in partial-year FY2024 [1].

EQT's Marketing and Trading desk links Upstream wells to premium buyers. Rather than selling 100% of gas at local hubs, EQT manages firm pipe capacity, underground storage, and long-term utility deals [1]. In July 2026, EQT also paid $77 million for Blackline Midstream's New England liquefied propane marine terminals. Per the FY2025 Form 10-K, no single customer exceeds 10% of revenue, yet ~94% of upstream accounts receivable (96% in 2024) came from non-end-user intermediaries and marketers [1]. Only ~49% of sales volume currently exits Appalachia on firm takeaway, leaving ~51% exposed to regional pricing, while 1.2 Bcf/d of 2027 MVP firm sales agreements depend on Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement project [1].

Concrete End-to-End Marketing & Storage Example: In a mild October, spot gas at Eastern Gas South often drops below $1.50/MMBtu. Rather than selling flush output into that weak market, EQT injects gas into its FERC-regulated storage fields in Pennsylvania and West Virginia [1, 2]. At the same time, it sells forward winter NYMEX futures or collars [1, 2]. When a January polar vortex hits the Mid-Atlantic—like Winter Storm Fern in Q1 2026—EQT pulls gas from storage at 3,000+ psia [3]. It ships those molecules down MVP into Virginia and serves peak utility demand at winter premiums [3, 8, 18].

book_paragraphs: To see why EQT looks nothing like the average shale driller, you and I need to trace a single molecule of methane from seven thousand feet beneath Greene County, Pennsylvania, all the way to a power plant in Virginia or an LNG tanker in the Gulf of Mexico. Most independent E&P companies only own the wellhead. The moment gas leaves their separator, they hand it—and a hefty slice of their margin—to third-party gatherers, processors, and pipeline operators.

EQT dismantled that tollbooth model. In its FY2025 Form 10-K, the company reports three distinct operating engines: Upstream, Gathering, and Transmission [1]. Together, they generated $8.64 billion in consolidated revenue and $3.25 billion in operating income across 2,382 Bcfe of sales volume [1, 2]. Think of Upstream as the factory floor, Gathering as the local conveyor belt, and Transmission as the interstate highway.

Let us walk through each piece in concrete terms. First, Upstream: EQT holds roughly 28.0 Tcfe of proved reserves, with 93% concentrated in the Marcellus Shale [1]. Its FY2025 commodity sales reached $7.73 billion at $3.19 per Mcfe realized, though 94% of upstream receivables sit with non-end-user marketers and ~51% of volume still clears inside Appalachia [1, 2].

book_subsections.title: The Midstream Tollbooth and the Global LNG Bridge
paragraphs: Now follow that molecule into the Gathering segment, which earned $836.7 million in operating income in 2025 [1]. Low-pressure wet gas cannot enter an interstate trunkline without dehydration and massive compression. Because EQT re-acquired Equitrans Midstream and bought XcL Midstream, 76% of its gathering revenue comes from moving its own gas—meaning the fee Upstream pays stays inside the corporate family—while the remaining 24% is pure third-party toll income from neighboring drillers [1].

Finally, the Transmission segment ($375.2 million operating income in 2025) moves gas out of the basin via FERC-regulated storage, the Hammerhead Pipeline, and the 2.0 Bcf/d Mountain Valley Pipeline [1, 18]. Instead of dumping gas at discounted local Appalachian hubs, EQT can ship molecules south to Virginia and the Carolinas, where utilities pay premium Zone 5 pricing.

And management is scaling its global export book well beyond initial headlines. Alongside the 2.5 MTPA NextDecade and Commonwealth LNG deals [11, 12], EQT's FY2025 Form 10-K reveals up to 6.5 MTPA in 20-year LNG offtake and tolling commitments starting in 2030–2031 (with 3.0 MTPA still awaiting developer FID) [1]. In Q3 2026, EQT added a 10-year LNG supply deal with Lithuania's Ignitis Group, expanded Gulf Coast salt-dome storage to 11 Bcf at Leaf River, and opened an expansion season for its 42-inch POWER Pipeline into Ohio.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Vertical integration in natural gas is not about empire-building; it is about controlling the basis spread. By owning the gathering header and interstate egress, EQT converts what used to be a third-party fixed expense into an internal profit center.

book_subsections.title: How Underground Storage and Commercial Arbitrage Work in Practice
paragraphs: Most investors think of a natural gas company as a simple drill-and-sell operation: punch a hole, turn a valve, collect whatever price is on the screen that morning. If you operated that way in Appalachia, you would get slaughtered every spring and autumn when heating demand vanishes and local prices sink.

Let us walk through how EQT's commercial desk actually monetizes its storage and pipeline network. Imagine it is October in southwestern Pennsylvania. Temperatures are sixty degrees, air conditioners are off, and furnaces are not yet running. Spot gas at the local Eastern Gas South hub is trading at a steep discount. Instead of selling its flush production into a buyer's market, EQT routes gas into its owned underground storage reservoirs—depleted porous rock formations sealed beneath impermeable caprock [1].

Three months later, in January, an Arctic cold front sweeps across Washington, D.C., Richmond, and Raleigh. Electric utilities scramble for baseload fuel as wind and solar output drops and coal plants strain. EQT opens its storage valves, pushes gas onto the Mountain Valley Pipeline, and delivers firm supply directly into Transco Zone 5 at peak winter pricing [8, 18]. Add the 2.5 MTPA of Gulf Coast LNG liquefaction capacity EQT locked up with NextDecade and Commonwealth LNG in September 2025 [11, 12], and you begin to see the full commercial architecture: EQT is no longer just a price-taking driller; it is an integrated energy merchant backed by 28.0 Tcfe of owned reserves [1].

book_subsections.title: Follow the Molecule: From Marcellus Wellhead to Gulf Coast LNG Tanker
paragraphs: Let us trace a single molecule of methane from a Marcellus pad in Greene County, Pennsylvania all the way to its final buyer, because that physical journey explains EQT's three reporting segments better than any accounting footnote. Deep underground—roughly 7,000 to 8,500 feet below the surface—horizontal laterals extending two to three miles crack open tight organic-rich shale. Once the gas reaches the surface separator, water and condensate are stripped out, and the raw gas enters EQT's Gathering segment.

In Gathering, low-pressure steel lines collect output from dozens of pads, compress it, and route it to processing or interstate interconnects. Because EQT owns the Equitrans gathering network, those gathering fees stay inside the consolidated family rather than leaking to an outside midstream operator. From there, molecules destined for Southeast utilities or Gulf Coast LNG terminals enter the Transmission segment—most notably the Mountain Valley Pipeline, which moves up to 2.0 Bcf/d southward into Virginia and the Carolinas, bypassing congested Appalachian bottlenecks.

Finally, EQT's Marketing and LNG agreements bridge the gap between Appalachian wellheads and global pricing. Instead of dumping every molecule at discounted local hubs like Eastern Gas South, EQT's firm transportation portfolio and long-term liquefaction agreements with partners like NextDecade and Commonwealth LNG allow it to capture premium Henry Hub and international netbacks.

book_subsections.title: Customer Reality: Utilities, Industrial Buyers & Global LNG Offtakers
paragraphs: Who actually writes the checks that fund EQT's $9.33 billion in trailing revenue? Three distinct customer cohorts sit on the other side of the meter. First are regulated Mid-Atlantic and Southeast electric and gas utilities—companies like Duke Energy and Dominion—that rely on Mountain Valley Pipeline deliveries for baseload power generation and winter heating.

Second are Gulf Coast LNG exporters and European buyers like Lithuania's Ignitis Group, who contract for Henry Hub-linked cargoes. Crucially, however, EQT's FY2025 Form 10-K reveals that 94% of its upstream accounts receivable are owed by non-end-user trading intermediaries rather than utilities, making counterparty credit discipline essential [1]. Third are emerging hyperscale data-center power developers in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and Virginia seeking reliable, low-cost natural gas generation.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A pure-play driller is a price-taker at the local hub. An integrated producer-midstream-LNG marketer controls where its molecules clear, giving it optionality across seasonal weather spikes and international arbitrage windows.
